g1|variants|shipment and transportation.family_title: Shipment and Transportation Integration in SAP OTC
g1|variants|shipment and transportation.summary: This family covers the integration variants between SAP Transportation Management (TM) and Order-to-Cash fulfillment in SAP S/4HANA. Variants differ based on whether transportation planning triggers outbound deliveries, uses basic shipping or advanced TM, and integrates via direct order integration or freight unit building.

variants.name: Order-Based Transportation with Delivery Integration
variants.when_used: Transportation planning is performed on sales orders or delivery requirements before delivery creation, common in complex freight forwarding.
variants.key_config: Activation of Enterprise Business Function /SCMTMS/INT and assignment of TM integration profile to sales document types.

variants.name: Delivery-Based Transportation Planning
variants.when_used: Outbound deliveries are created first from sales orders, and transportation planning is executed using the delivery documents.
variants.key_config: Shipping point determination, delivery type configuration, and activation of TM delivery integration profile in LE-SHP.

variants.name: Basic Shipping and Transportation (LE-TRA / LE-SHP)
variants.when_used: Traditional logistics execution without Advanced TM, using shipment documents for route scheduling and freight costs.
variants.key_config: Transportation connection point routing, shipment types, and route determination in sales order.

variants.name: Direct Sales Order Fulfillment without Advanced TM
variants.when_used: Standard OTC processing where deliveries and billing occur directly from sales orders without external or advanced transport planning.
variants.key_config: Standard schedule line category configuration, delivery creation via VL01N/VL10G, and billing via VF01.

g1|core|shipment and transportation|orde.title: Order-Based Transportation with Delivery Integration (Advanced TM DOI)
g1|core|shipment and transportation|orde.story: We plan how to ship goods to our customers right after the sales order is saved, before making any delivery. In SAP S/4HANA, the sales order talks to Transportation Management (TM) to create freight units, we plan the trucks, and then we create deliveries based on that transportation plan. When the driver leaves, billing happens against the delivery. If this process stops, trucks do not get booked and customer orders stay stuck without delivery creation.
g1|core|shipment and transportation|orde.why_business_needs_it: Advanced Transportation Management integrated with Sales and Distribution ensures efficient freight consolidation and carrier selection before warehouse picking begins. This directly reduces freight costs and prevents redundant warehouse tasks for unassigned orders.

g1|core|shipment and transportation|deli.title: Delivery-Based Transportation Planning (SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash Integration with Transportation Management)
g1|core|shipment and transportation|deli.story: Imagine a giant delivery truck that needs to pick up toys from a warehouse and drop them off at a store, but the computer has to carefully plan which boxes go into which truck so nothing gets squished. In SAP S/4HANA, outbound deliveries are created first, which then trigger the creation of freight units that transport planners organize into freight orders and freight bookings within embedded Transportation Management (TM).
g1|core|shipment and transportation|deli.why_business_needs_it: The business requires systematic transportation planning to consolidate shipments, optimize freight costs, and ensure on-time delivery while maintaining seamless integration with Order-to-Cash (OTC) billing processes. Without this integration, companies face manual freight booking errors, unoptimized truck capacities, and delayed customer invoicing due to disconnected transportation milestones.

g1|core|shipment and transportation|basi.title: Basic Shipping and Transportation via LE-TRA (Classic)
g1|core|shipment and transportation|basi.story: Just like putting your birthday presents into a cardboard box and hiring a delivery truck to drop them off at your friend's house, the system packs sales items and plans a shipping route. Specifically, Logistics Execution Transportation (LE-TRA) coordinates outbound shipments, carrier assignment, and freight documentation based on the outbound delivery document.
g1|core|shipment and transportation|basi.why_business_needs_it: It ensures that goods are efficiently consolidated into shipments, assigned to carriers, and tracked until delivery, which directly drives customer satisfaction and accurate freight cost accounting. Without this, organizations cannot properly plan transport capacity or bill customers for freight.

g1|core|shipment and transportation|dire.title: Direct Sales Order Fulfillment without Advanced TM
g1|core|shipment and transportation|dire.story: A customer orders goods, and the system instantly packs and ships them directly from the warehouse without needing complex transportation planning. In technical terms, this scenario processes customer sales orders through the Logistics Execution Shipping (LE-SHP) component, creating immediate outbound deliveries without Advanced Transportation Management (Advanced TM) integration, followed by delivery-related billing.
g1|core|shipment and transportation|dire.why_business_needs_it: Companies need a streamlined fulfillment path for standard sales orders where external freight optimization is unnecessary, allowing fast order-to-delivery cycles with minimal overhead. It ensures that standard orders automatically trigger outbound processing and billing without requiring manual transportation planning units or freight tender steps.

g1|panel|shipment and transportation.otc_impact: Shipment and transportation sits at the critical physical hand-off between outbound delivery creation and billing generation in Order-to-Cash, determining how goods move from plant to customer and dictating freight cost accrual. It transforms standard order fulfillment by consolidating deliveries into shipments, executing route scheduling, and updating billing documents with freight charges. When transportation breaks, outbound deliveries get stuck in transit status, billing blocks prevent invoice generation, and customer service KPIs like on-time delivery plummet.

panel_qa.question: How do we choose between basic LE-SHP shipping and advanced Transportation Management integration for our outbound deliveries?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: This decision hinges on operational complexity and freight management requirements. We use basic shipping via Logistics Execution Shipping (LE-SHP) when route determination and simple delivery scheduling suffice without complex freight cost calculation or carrier selection. We integrate Delivery-Based Transportation Planning with Advanced Transportation Management (TM) when multi-leg routing, container optimization, and carrier tendering are mandatory. Technically, LE-SHP relies on route determination in transaction OVR1, whereas TM integration triggers freight units via PP/DS or direct delivery creation in transaction VL01N. The leadership value is avoiding over-engineering simple distribution while ensuring scalable freight optimization for complex global networks. Moving forward, SAP strategic direction mandates Advanced TM over legacy LE-TRA. The weak answer is to install Advanced TM for a single-plant local operation that only needs basic parcel tracking.
panel_qa.trap: The weak answer is to install Advanced TM for a single-plant local operation that only needs basic parcel tracking.

panel_qa.question: What stops billing documents from being created when transportation execution is incomplete?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Billing document generation is halted by delivery blocks or incomplete transportation status when shipping requirements are not fully met. We enforce this through billing relevance settings on delivery types and transportation completion checks in copy control. Technically, we set the delivery-related billing relevance indicator in transaction VOV8 and assign copy control requirements in transaction VTFL. The leadership value is preventing premature invoicing of un-shipped goods, mitigating revenue leakage and customer disputes. Next, we ensure batch jobs monitor delivery status logs via transaction /SCWM/MON or transaction VL06O. The weak answer is to remove billing blocks entirely to speed up monthly revenue recognition regardless of shipping status.
